title: Fire the fall-through warn once, and say role where the surface means role
action: Three review-verified fixes. (1) prepare.rs:98 cell_role_list: never repeat the head - cell_role_list(code) currently returns [code, code, generation] so the warn fires twice and its first copy names the name that just failed; dedup so the list holds distinct names in order (code -> [code, generation]; read -> [read, extraction, generation]; test -> [test, code, generation]). RED FIRST for this one: a test asserting cell_role_list(code) contains no duplicate, shown failing on unfixed code, output quoted in the cap. Check call sites for assumptions about list length. (2) registry_payload.json, the dispatch.prepare TOP-LEVEL description: rewrite the tier-language sentences - kind cell resolves the cell-role-headed ordered list ([<cell role>, code, generation], read cells via read), gather stays the read-only default, reviewer resolves the review role falling through to generation, advisor unchanged. Keep the rest of the prose. Edit as DATA (one-line JSON, reproduce serialization exactly, round-trip check before writing). (3) state_group/workers.rs:78: the refusal opens with: invalid tier - change the opening words to name a ROLE (e.g. invalid role recorded under the tier flag) while leaving the flag spelling, the persisted key, and the recorded rationale at workers.rs:154-190 untouched.

truths: cell_role_list returns no duplicate name for any role input, pinned by a test shown red first
A role equal to a tail name still resolves exactly as before - only the duplicate is gone
The dispatch.prepare registry description mentions the ordered role list and no longer claims kind cell resolves the generation tier
registry_payload.json still parses, command count unchanged, serialization byte-style preserved
The workers refusal no longer calls the value an invalid tier; its FIX line and the persisted key stay exactly as recorded
registry_dispatch tests stay green in both directions

trace.outcome: the fall-through warn fires once per dispatch, the registry speaks role language, the worker refusal says role
deviations: sync-ack: workers.rs is a wording-only change inside a refusal string; the flag, key, and recorded rationale are untouched, so no owned skill has anything to update.

Three wording assertions retargeted with the fix.
